turns.user: I run a 38k Handysize. Everyone is shouting about the BDI. What did *my* market actually do last week?
turns.answer:
## Your 38k Handysize market, Baltic Week 36 (ended Fri 4 Sep 2026)

The BDI headlines you're hearing are a Capesize story, and your segment is a different, much flatter market. Here's what actually happened to the 38k Handysize last week.

**The index and the TCA (your exact benchmark)**
- **BHSI closed the week at ~900**, up **2.2% week-on-week** from 881 the prior Friday (Xclusiv week-36 report, data as of 4 Sep 2026).
- The Baltic **Handysize 7TC timecharter average closed at ~$16,200/day**, up roughly **$300/day** on the week (same source). The BHSI basket is a 38,000-dwt vessel, so this is directly your number.
- Year-to-date context: BHSI averages ~796 in 2026 vs 661 in 2025 and 704 in 2024 — your segment is running about 20% above last year, but it is not in the same orbit as the Capesize move.

**Route-level moves (Xclusiv, week 36)**
- Brazil → Continent: **+$900/day to ~$23,350/day** (the strongest leg).
- US Gulf → Continent: **+$900/day to ~$15,814/day**.
- Skaw–Passero → Boston/Galveston: +$500/day to ~$11,221/day.
- SE Asia → Singapore/Japan ~$18,169/day; China/Korea/Japan round ~$17,281/day; NoPac→SE Asia ~$17,819/day — each up only ~$100/day.

**Baltic Exchange weekly narrative (via Daily Cargo News, 4 Sep)** described the market as **steady-to-firmer**, opening September positionally firm across both basins. Continent/Med activity was limited but firming late-week; the US Gulf and South Atlantic had the healthier momentum on a balanced cargo-to-tonnage list. Representative fixtures: a **39,000-dwt open Mobile, 15 Sep, trip Panama City → UK-Continent (pellets) at $18,000/day**; a **38,000-dwt Recalada → WC South America in the high-$20,000s**; a **43,000-dwt open Acajutla mid-Sep, via NoPac, redelivery Singapore-Japan at $17,000**. Period: a **40,000-dwt fixed for one year at $17,500/day**.

**One contradictory read you should keep on file:** Dry Cargo International's Week 36 desk described a *slower* week, with **BHSI and the weighted TCA edging down** after more than a month in positive territory, and the Continent/Med surge showing softening signs — with a **38,000-dwt open Manila fixed to South China in the high-$7,000s**. That's a materially lower spot level than the Baltic/Xclusiv read on USG/Atlantic. I'd treat the two as reflecting different basins and day-points, not average them.

**Bottom line:** Last week your 38k market was steady-to-firmer, +2–3% on the index, with the HS7 average around $16,200/day and best money in the Atlantic/Brazil leg. The BDI at 3,620 (near five-year highs) is a Capesize/C5 phenomenon — BCI was ~6,400 with the C5TC at ~$54,800/day (Xclusiv) — and none of that demand surge is showing up in Handysize earnings. Your market is a modest, uneven uptick, not the rally the headlines imply.

*Data-as-of: Baltic week 36 (Fri 4 Sep 2026) for the segment prints; BDI/BCI spot as of 9 Sep via OilPriceAPI. BHSI is not available in the OilPriceAPI catalog, so segment figures are from Xclusiv's week-36 report and the Baltic Exchange weekly narrative.*

turns.user: Does the BDI even include Handysize? If not, why do my investors keep sending me BDI charts?
turns.answer:
**No — the BDI has not included Handysize since 1 March 2018.** That's a methodology change, not a detail, and it matters for how you read your investor's charts.

**What the BDI actually is (Baltic Exchange, current methodology):**
- The BDI is a weighted composite of the **timecharter averages of three segments only: Capesize 40%, Panamax 30%, Supramax 30%** (Baltic Exchange Indices page, published 9 Sep 2026).
- From 1 March 2018 the Baltic re-weighted the index and **removed the Handysize timecharter average entirely** (Baltic Exchange press release, original statement by CEO Mark Jackson). Pre-2018, the BDI was an equal 25% blend of Cape/Panamax/Supramax/Handysize, so yes — Handysize *used* to be a component. It isn't anymore.
- The Exchange's justification at the time: external research put Handysize's contribution to dry bulk trade at only **~10%** (by fleet composition, utilisation and cargo moved on AIS/import-export data), so its exclusion made "no statistical difference."
- **Your market is the BHSI** — a standalone Baltic index, not a BDI component. Its benchmark vessel is a non-scrubber 38,200-dwt geared bulk carrier, ~10.5m SSW draft, 15 years max age — essentially your ship. The relevant earnings line is the **HS7TC** (7-route weighted timecharter average), which closed last week at ~$16,200/day. That's the number to watch, not the BDI.

## Why investors keep sending you BDI charts

Four overlapping reasons, none of which is that it measures your market:

1. **It's the only dry bulk index on their screens.** The BDI has a continuous series back to 1985 (as the Baltic Freight Index), it's quoted daily by Reuters, CNBC, Bloomberg and the shipping press (Hellenic runs the print every trading day), and every generalist dashboard carries it. The BHSI is a niche subscription feed that most portfolio-level tools simply don't include.

2. **It's the tradable one.** The BDI is the settlement basis for the dry bulk **FFA (forward freight agreement) complex** — it's the freight market's tradeable, hedgeable, liquid price. Investors who track it are watching a derivatives market, not your fixture levels. Handysize has no liquid FFA market; that alone explains why the headline index dominates.

3. **It's a macro proxy, not an earnings estimate.** Economists and equity desks use the BDI as a leading indicator for global industrial activity — iron ore into China, coal, bauxite. When it prints 3,620 (near five-year highs), that's signalling a commodity-cycle story. It is not signalling your cash flows.

4. **They're sending you "the market's beta."** For a shipping equity or fund investor, the BDI is the standard market benchmark against which an owner's performance gets judged. The problem: because the BDI is 40% Capesize, its current move is almost entirely a C5 iron-ore/bauxite rally — a market with **zero correlation** to a 38k Handysize trading the US Gulf–Continent, Brazil and Pacific-and-trades. Your last week was +2.2% on the BHSI to ~900 with HS7 at ~$16,200/day; the BDI's 3,620 tells you nothing about that.

**Practical counsel:** next time they send the chart, send back the two-line answer — *"BDI hasn't contained Handysize since March 2018; my benchmark is BHSI (38,200-dwt vessel spec, HS7TC). Last week HS7 averaged $16.2k/day, up ~$300 on the week."* If they want a single-page chart series, put BHSI + HS7TC on it next to the BDI and let them see the two markets diverge — it's the fastest way to get off the headline composite and on to your actual earnings.
